data.current_description: Puts one address into the sequence; the first step is due delay_minutes after enrolment. Works for any active automation whatever its trigger kind, and the address needs no contact record (though without one it has no tags, so required_tags keep it out). Outcomes: 201 enrolled. 200 enrolled false with reason already_enrolled: safe to retry. 200 with previously_enrolled: the automation's reenrollment is never and this person has already been through it. 200 with suppressed, unsubscribed_from_topic, exit_tag or required_tag_missing: deliberately excluded by an automatic exit; do not work around it. 409 invalid_state with reason not_active, no_steps or topic_missing: the automation cannot take anyone until its definition or status is fixed; retrying will not help. Checks run in the order not_active, no_steps, suppressed, topic_missing, unsubscribed_from_topic, tag rules, previously_enrolled, already_enrolled. The calling key's guardrails decide whether it may enrol at all: a key that holds its sends for approval is refused outright (the steps would later send with no approval), and a key with a recipient allowlist may only enrol addresses on it. The key's daily cap is not checked and later steps do not count against it.

data.current_summary: Approve or reject a held message
data.current_description: Decides one held send. Only an API key without guardrails that did not make the draft can decide: an OAuth access token, the key that made the draft, and any key with a guardrail (requires_approval, allowed_recipients or a daily_send_limit) are refused with 403 forbidden, so an agent cannot release its own mail, another held agent's, or mail its own limits would not allow. A person in the dashboard can always decide. Rejecting marks the message canceled. Approving first re-checks suppressions and topic opt-outs for every recipient (dropping anyone who left; if no To address remains nothing is sent, the message is recorded rejected, and the response carries skipped and reason) and the plan allowance. Then, if the draft carried a scheduled_at still in the future, the message is put on that schedule (status scheduled, scheduled_at in the response): approving does not bring the send forward. Otherwise it is sent now and scheduled_at is null. The approval is recorded as approved only once the release works: on any failure the approval stays pending with the reason, and can be approved again once the cause is fixed (until it expires). Only one decision lands: 409 invalid_state means it was decided or expired, do not retry; 409 approval_in_progress means another decision is releasing it right now, check the list again in a moment. The key's allowlist and daily cap are not re-checked.
data.description_suggestion: Approves or rejects a pending email approval. Approval requires an API key without guardrails that did not create the draft (OAuth tokens can always decide). Rejecting marks the message as canceled. Approving re-validates all recipients against current suppressions and topic opt-outs, dropping unsubscribed addresses; if no recipients remain, the message is rejected with skipped status. If the draft has a future scheduled_at, the message is scheduled for that time; otherwise it sends immediately. The approval is recorded only after the send succeeds; on failure it remains pending and can be retried. Returns 409 invalid_state if already decided or expired (do not retry), or 409 approval_in_progress if another decision is in flight. The key's allowlist and daily cap are not re-checked during approval.
